paragraphs.text: A third-party service provider breach exposed personal and marketing data of Chase, Visa, and Mastercard customers, while a Linux KVM hypervisor flaw allowed cross-tenant memory access on shared AMD hosts and a VMware vCenter zero-day was actively exploited for administrative access. These events indicate that supplier compromises and hypervisor vulnerabilities can bypass tenant isolation and directly impact sensitive financial data. Control owners should prioritize supplier assurance reviews and cloud infrastructure patching verification.

An N-able server breach caused a global outage of email security services, spreadsheet-based password tracking left administrators blind to credential risks, and Microsoft began automatically upgrading unmanaged devices to Windows 11 26H2 without IT oversight. These developments highlight gaps in supplier incident response, credential governance, and change control for unmanaged endpoints. Owners should confirm supplier notification obligations, enforce centralized password management, and validate device management policies.
